site.name: Blue Bird Mine & Caribou Ranch Mining Complex
site.location: Caribou Ranch Open Space, west of Nederland
site.componentDetail: Historic Blue Bird silver mine complex at Caribou Ranch, including mine shafts, ore-cart tracks, surviving bunkhouse/company-house structures, and the foundation of its mill.
overview: The Blue Bird Mine was established in 1871 at what is now Caribou Ranch Open Space west of Nederland. It was primarily a silver mine and became part of the broader Caribou-area mining boom that transformed western Boulder County in the late nineteenth century.

By 1881 a mill had been developed at the Blue Bird. The surviving complex preserves mine shafts, ore-cart tracks, a bunkhouse, mining-company house, smokehouse and the foundation of the mill, making it one of Boulder County's strongest surviving mine-complex landscapes.

timeline.text: The Blue Bird Mine was established and developed as a primarily silver-producing operation in the Caribou mining area.
A mill had been developed at the Blue Bird Mine, adding an ore-processing component to the property.
The Denver, Boulder & Western narrow-gauge railroad—better known as the Switzerland Trail—served the area; Blue Bird became a tourist stop on the Eldora Line in 1905.
Mining continued intermittently at the Blue Bird and surrounding Caribou Ranch landscape while the property also developed ranching and later cultural uses.
Boulder County preserves the Blue Bird Mine complex within Caribou Ranch Open Space and interprets its surviving mining structures and landscape for visitors.

moreHistory: Boulder County's management plan identifies the Blue Bird as a historic silver mine developed by the Sanata La Saria Mining Company of Colorado and documents the addition of a mill by 1881.

The mine's later connection to the Switzerland Trail added a transportation and tourism layer to the site. In 1905, Blue Bird became a tourist destination on the newly completed Eldora Line while the railroad also served western Boulder County mining properties.

The Remnant location point represents the historic Blue Bird complex rather than a safe mine entrance. Surviving shafts and industrial remains can be hazardous; visitors should stay on designated public routes and respect seasonal closures and open-space rules.
